_what: The WAL trap from docs/RUNBOOK.md, reproduced again on this run: a backup that copies only ledger.sqlite archives a nearly empty database. Sizes in bytes.

_midRunObservation._what: Observed directly during the run (at 18:16 local, while one registry process held the database and no driver had closed a connection since): the main file was 4,096 bytes with 3,230,112 bytes of live data in the -wal. This is the RUNBOOK's trap in its severe form. It is recorded as an observation with its time rather than re-measured, because by the end of the run the driver processes had each closed their own connection and checkpointed most of it — which is why the numbers below are much less dramatic.

_reading: The trap is real and its severity is not constant: it is worst when a long-lived writer holds the only connection. Checkpointing before archiving is still the rule, because the operator cannot tell from the file sizes which case they are in.
